attributes.residual: SAME MECHANISM AS fn_80051164, AND THE 'SOLVE ONCE, APPLY TWICE' PREMISE HOLDS FOR THE DIAGNOSIS BUT NOT FOR THE CURE. Baseline real 22, insns 43/43, multiset 12t. All three differing loops are the r0-role swap described in claim.law.r0-homed-address-temp-forces-the-indexed-store-form.20260901.v1: target `add r4,r5,r3` + `stw r0,DISP(r4)` at DISP 2860/1324/1176 with byte-IV strides 20/48/36; ours `addi r0,r3,DISP` + `stwx r4,r5,r0`. THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE THAT SOURCE FORM IS NOT THE LEVER LIVES IN THIS FUNCTION: the source ALREADY uses correct typed struct-array indexing (st->que[i].f0, st->voice[i].flags, st->trk[i].f0, with strides that are genuine sizeof values) - i.e. it is already in the shape the superseded record prescribed as the fix - and still emits stwx; meanwhile this function's FOURTH loop, written as a walked pointer (c->f0 = -1; ... c++), matches the target byte-for-byte. So neither 'typed array index' nor 'raw byte cursor' predicts the store form. AXIS KILLED: hoisting the three stored constants into explicit locals (int zero = 0; int neg = -1;) to change which value the allocator parks in r0 measured NEUTRAL at real 22 with the multiset unmoved. Do not re-open by respelling the index or the constant; the next honest move is the WebFrank addressing-mode rule described in the companion law, or a register-pressure change from an unrelated part of the TU.
